subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Unhandled Promise rejection: `ContentstackLivePreview.init({...}).then(() => { ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange(handleEntryChange); })` has no `.catch()` handler. The previous code had a try/catch that swallowed init failures ("Live preview SDK init is a no-op outside preview mode; swallow"). This violates the TypeScript strict compliance criterion: no unhandled Promise rejections. If `init()` rejects outside preview mode, the unhandled rejection will surface as a runtime error.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a `.catch()` handler: `ContentstackLivePreview.init({ stackSdk: Stack as any, enable: true, ssr: false }).then(() => { ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange(handleEntryChange); }).catch(() => { /* Live preview SDK init is a no-op outside preview mode; swallow. */ });`

issues.description: The `onEntryChange` callback does not re-fetch draft entry data as prescribed by the root cause analysis. The plan explicitly states: 'In the onEntryChange callback, re-fetch the changed entry using the same Stack ContentType/Entry pattern used by ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery (line 185) and update React state (useState) that feeds the ContentstackContext.Provider value.' The implementation just does `setLivePreviewEntry({ __livePreviewUpdatedAt: Date.now() })` — a timestamp bump with no actual entry data. The `livePreviewEntry` field in the context is `{ __livePreviewUpdatedAt: number }`, not draft content. Components reading `page.0.title` via `useContent().getContentByKey()` still get the server-rendered published data because the `page` field in the context never changes. The verification criteria ('the rendered Homepage shows the draft entry content instead of the previously published content') cannot be met without delivering draft content through the context.
issues.suggestedFix: In `handleEntryChange`, re-fetch the changed entry using the existing `getSingleEntry` / `getSinglePageEntry` pattern from pageService.ts (which delegates to `ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery`). Store the fetched draft entry in React state and feed it into the `ContentstackContext.Provider` value so all `useContent` consumers re-render with draft data. The callback should update the `page` field (or a parallel draft field) with actual entry content, not a timestamp.

issues.description: Unnecessary structural change: `ContentstackContext.Provider` was moved from the outermost wrapper position to inside `ErrorBoundary`, and `CommonAnalytics` was moved outside the context. This restructure was not prescribed by the plan — the plan only prescribed adding the `onEntryChange` callback and updating the context value. The original structure (context as outermost wrapper) could have been preserved by simply updating the `value` prop to include `livePreviewEntry` and `setLivePreviewEntry`. This change increases the diff size and risks unintended side effects with component tree ordering.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the original component tree structure with `ContentstackContext.Provider` as the outermost wrapper. Simply update its `value` prop to include `livePreviewEntry` and `setLivePreviewEntry` alongside the existing `...pageProps` spread.

issues.description: `livePreviewEntry?: any` and `setLivePreviewEntry?: (entry: any) => void` use untyped `any` with eslint-disable comments. While the comments technically satisfy the 'no untyped any without explanatory comment' rule, the actual state type in `_app.tsx` is `{ __livePreviewUpdatedAt: number }` — there is a type mismatch between the context interface and the actual state. A proper interface type would be safer and more maintainable.
issues.suggestedFix: Define a typed interface for the live preview entry (e.g., `ILivePreviewEntry { __livePreviewUpdatedAt: number }` or the actual entry shape after re-fetching is implemented) and use it in the context interface instead of `any`.

issues.description: `CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST` default was changed from `"preview.contentstack.com"` to `""` without clear justification. This means if the env var is not set, the `live_preview.host` config will be an empty string, which may cause the SDK to malfunction or use an unexpected default. This change was not prescribed by the plan.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the default value `"preview.contentstack.com"` or document why the empty string default is preferred.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: package.json now declares "@contentstack/live-preview-utils": "^4.4.5" (line 85), but the lockfile contains NO entry for it — verified programmatically: packages[''].dependencies['@contentstack/live-preview-utils'] is undefined, packages['node_modules/@contentstack/live-preview-utils'] is undefined, and the legacy dependencies section has no entry. The diff actively REMOVED the lockfile entries for the package and its transitive deps (@preact/compat, @preact/signals, deepsignal, get-xpath, goober, lodash-es, mustache, uuid@14) while the manifest still requires them. `npm ci` will fail with EUSAGE (lock out of sync with package.json), breaking every clean install and CI build.
issues.suggestedFix: Run `npm install` after editing package.json so package-lock.json is regenerated with the @contentstack/live-preview-utils@^4.4.5 entry and its transitive dependency tree restored; commit both files together.

issues.description: handleEntryChange does not implement the prescribed producer behavior. The plan of record requires the onEntryChange callback to re-fetch the changed entry (reusing the Stack ContentType/Entry pattern from ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery) and push the draft entry data into React state so ContentstackContext consumers re-render with draft content. Instead the callback ignores the entry entirely and stores only { __livePreviewUpdatedAt: Date.now() } — no draft data ever reaches the context, and setLivePreviewEntry is never called with entry content. The verification criteria 'rendered Homepage/Discover Article shows the draft entry content instead of the previously published content' are therefore not demonstrably met: a timestamp bump cannot make useContent() consumers render draft fields.
issues.suggestedFix: In the onEntryChange callback, re-fetch the changed entry via the existing Stack/ContentstackFactory query pattern and call setLivePreviewEntry(entryData) with the actual draft entry, so the context value carries the updated content to all useContent consumers.

issues.description: The diff deletes the entire 329-line spec file (9 it() blocks) that the pipeline shipped to reproduce/verify this story — including the no-preview-regression, successive-entry-change, gated-page, and SDK-init-failure scenarios. Total test count is decreased and the story's verification evidence is removed. (Flagged as major rather than blocker only because test authorship is owned by the test-writer agent; the coverage gate should confirm replacement coverage exists.)
issues.suggestedFix: Do not delete the shipped spec in the implementer change; leave test updates to the test-writer agent, or restore the file.

issues.description: The provider nesting was restructured: ContentstackContext.Provider moved from the outermost wrapper to inside ErrorBoundary, and CommonAnalytics moved outside ErrorBoundary. This removes a guarantee the previous structure gave — the error fallback (ClientSideErrorFallback) and CommonAnalytics previously rendered inside the Contentstack context and could rely on it; now any context consumer in the fallback or analytics renders with an empty default context. This reordering is also unrelated to the prescribed fix (the plan only required adding the onEntryChange subscription and context updater).
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the original nesting (ContentstackContext.Provider outermost, ErrorBoundary and CommonAnalytics inside it) and limit the change to adding the live-preview state and context value fields.

issues.description: `stackSdk: Stack as any` is an untyped any cast with no explanatory comment or eslint-disable (the previous version's eslint-disable-next-line was removed in the rewrite), violating the project's TypeScript strict-compliance criterion.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-add `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` with a brief note that the SDK's stackSdk type does not match the contentstack.Stack type, or type the cast properly.

issues.description: The single react import was split into two import statements from 'react' (useEffect/ComponentType on one line, useCallback/useState on another) — pure churn that may trip no-duplicate-imports lint rules. Similarly, package.json appends @contentstack/live-preview-utils at the end of dependencies (out of alphabetical order) and silently downgrades it from ^4.5.0 to ^4.4.5 with no justification, and the contentstack.ts hunk is a no-op reorder of two destructured env vars.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep one combined react import; restore alphabetical placement of the dependency; document or revert the ^4.5.0 → ^4.4.5 downgrade; drop the cosmetic destructuring reorder in contentstack.ts.
